summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked from this environment, so today's evidence is Hacker News only and the report is shorter than usual. The strongest themes: paid Proton users hunting for an exit after leadership backlash, supply-chain worries around editor extension marketplaces and web-app updates, and distrust of AI-prepared tax returns.

ideas.title: Email Switch Kit
ideas.oneLiner: A guided migration planner for moving off Proton (or any mail host): export, import, DNS cutover, forwarding and a checklist of every account that uses the old address.
ideas.problem: Long-time paid Proton users say they are looking for alternatives after the CEO's public statements, but moving a decade of mail, contacts, calendars and logins is a multi-tool chore. Proton's export route needs a separate export app plus the new provider's MBOX importer, and nobody tracks which services still point at the old address.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded paying email users, small teams of 2–10 people choosing between Fastmail, Tuta, Zoho and Posteo, and people who own a custom domain.
ideas.monetization: Free checklist and planner; ₹/$9 one-time 'migration pass' for the account-inventory scanner, or $29 for small teams.
mvp: Pick source and destination provider and get a step-by-step personalised runbook (export, import, calendars, contacts)
Paste in or import a password-manager CSV or inbox sender list to build an inventory of accounts to update
Custom-domain DNS cutover helper (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC records with a copy-paste diff)
30-day forwarding and 'still receiving at old address' tracker with reminders
Side-by-side provider comparison (jurisdiction, protocols, price, export support)

competitors.name: Fastmail migration guide
competitors.gap: Covers only the mail import into Fastmail; the export is a separate Proton app and calendars and contacts are manual uploads. It does not help find which accounts to update.

competitors.name: Proton Easy Switch
competitors.gap: Moves mail into Proton, not out of it.

ideas.title: Extension Provenance Check
ideas.oneLiner: A CLI and editor plugin that verifies every installed VS Code or Cursor extension really comes from the publisher it claims, and alerts on look-alikes and unexpected updates.
ideas.problem: After the Cursor marketplace incident that shipped a fake Anthropic-branded extension, developers point out that Open VSX has weak publisher verification and no package signing, so they cannot tell an authentic extension from an impostor.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers on Cursor, VSCodium, Windsurf and other Open VSX-based editors; security-conscious teams.
ideas.monetization: Free CLI; $5/month per developer or $49/month per team for continuous monitoring, an org allowlist and Slack alerts.
mvp: Scan installed extensions and compare publisher, repo URL and hash against the upstream VS Code Marketplace and GitHub releases
Flag extensions whose publisher differs between marketplaces, or that are brand-new look-alikes
Alert when an installed extension updates, with a diff of manifest permissions and activation events
Team allowlist file checked in to the repo with CI check
Weekly digest of newly reported malicious extension IDs

competitors.name: vsix-audit (Trail of Bits)
competitors.gap: A CLI that runs detection modules on a single extension; it needs Node 22, has no continuous monitoring, and does not check cross-marketplace publisher mismatches.

competitors.name: SafeDep vet
competitors.gap: General dependency scanner with an extension option; no team allowlists or update diffs.

ideas.title: Pinned Web App Guard
ideas.oneLiner: A browser extension that lets you pin a web app to a known-good JavaScript release and warns before an unreviewed update runs.
ideas.problem: After a crypto-exchange style web-app attack, commenters say there is no practical way to lock a web app to a reproducible build or only accept updates signed by an offline key. Subresource integrity covers only separately hosted resources.
ideas.targetUsers: Users of wallets, banking and password web apps, and developers who want to offer verified web clients.
ideas.monetization: Free for users; $29/month for app publishers who want a signed-manifest registry and verification badge.
mvp: Hash all scripts a chosen site loads and store them as the pinned release
Block or warn on any changed script, showing a diff summary
Publisher-signed manifest support (offline signing key) for opt-in sites
Per-site allow update button with a changelog link
Export/import pins for teams

competitors.name: Code Verify (Meta)
competitors.gap: Built around Meta properties and a Cloudflare-hosted reference; third-party sites are not supported out of the box.

competitors.name: code-verify fork (AadarshSree)
competitors.gap: You must clone and build it yourself, and the original audit endpoint is not public.

sources.title: Web-app attack thread
sources.quote: Fundamentally: There is no way to lock webapps to reproducible builds. Except: IPFS could do it but IPFS has been very very poorly maintained.

sources.title: Web-app attack thread
sources.quote: There is no way to, for instance, only allow updates to a PWA from files signed by an offline key.

sources.title: Web-app attack thread
sources.quote: Fundamentally: There is no way to lock webapps to reproducible builds. One could absolutely use subresource integrity to lock one's reference to a vendor's subresource to a specific version.

ideas.title: Tax Return Second Opinion
ideas.oneLiner: Upload your prepared tax return or ITR plus source documents and get a field-by-field mismatch and deduction check before you file.
ideas.problem: People are using LLMs to prepare taxes or to double-check an accountant's work, and finding that human-prepared returns can be riddled with wrong fields. A CPA says the realistic use is transcription and review, not end-to-end filing. Consumers have no cheap, private cross-check tool.
ideas.targetUsers: Salaried individuals and freelancers filing their own or accountant-prepared returns, starting with Indian ITR filers.
ideas.monetization: Free scan summary; ₹299–₹499 per return for the full report with source citations; CA referral fees.
mvp: Upload return PDF or JSON plus Form 16, AIS/26AS and bank interest statements
Extract values and flag fields that do not match the source documents
Check for common missed deductions and wrong regime choice
Output a short list of questions to take back to your accountant
Delete-after-processing privacy mode with local-only option

competitors.name: TaxGPT Agent Andrew
competitors.gap: Aimed at professional firms; priced and designed for preparers, not individuals.

sources.title: AI tax preparation thread
sources.quote: I prepared my taxes this year using Astra + Codex. ... They sent it back for final review, and I had Codex check it; it was riddled with errors. The refund was nearly $2k lower than it should have been

sources.title: AI tax preparation thread
sources.quote: As a veteran tax CPA, I think LLMs can be very good at preparing taxes but I would not trust them to complete a tax return start to finish.

ideas.title: Pseudonym Exposure Check
ideas.oneLiner: After a site breach, check whether an email or username can be tied to your real identity across other services and get a plan to separate them.
ideas.problem: After the AO3 security incident, commenters worry that emails containing real names plus reading history could be linked back to people, and some predict someone will build a lookup tool to expose them. Pseudonymous users want to know how linkable their accounts are.
ideas.targetUsers: Fandom writers and readers, hobby communities and anyone keeping a pseudonymous online identity.
ideas.monetization: Free check; $3/month for alerts and a guided alias-email rollout.
mvp: Check an email against public breach lists and flag when it contains a real name
Scan your username for reuse across popular sites
Generate a step list for creating separate aliases and changing the login email
Alert when a new breach includes your address
Plain-language explainer of what a breached hashed password means

competitors.name: Have I Been Pwned
competitors.gap: Tells you a breach exists but not how linkable your pseudonym is or how to separate identities.
